checks.invariant: A caller's glob pattern costs time roughly proportional to path length × pattern length, and it cannot block the event loop shared by other agents.
checks.result: Confirmed. _translate turns each '*' into a backtracking [^/]* with no cap on how many wildcards a pattern may contain. A '[...]' class makes the SQL LIKE prefilter fall back to an empty prefix, so every row in the mount becomes a candidate. The regex runs inline on the event loop, before view.shows. Doubling n multiplies the time by about 2^k (about 14x at k=4, n=64 to 128), so the cost is O(n^k). The longest event-loop stall roughly equals the full glob time.

checks.invariant: Grep's WALL_TIME_BUDGET bounds the cost of matching grep's globs/globs_not.
checks.result: Not bounded. The glob gates (passes_gates, the same compile_filter regex) run inline per candidate, and the deadline is checked only between stages. This is the same root cause as the glob finding (variant), capped at CANDIDATE_BUDGET=25,000 candidates per call.

checks.invariant: Grep output in lines mode is bounded by the size of the body, regardless of the context-line arguments.
checks.result: Not bounded, per source. extend_context gives every hit line its own span of up to before/after lines (params allow up to 2^31-1), and python.rs copies each span into a separate PyBytes. Overlapping contexts are never merged, so output can reach about (hit lines) × (body bytes). Not run locally.

checks.invariant: A huge glean limit does not allocate memory before any rows are read.
checks.result: Holds. vector_depth = 10×limit only feeds SQL LIMIT. cosine_topk and lexical score do not pre-allocate by k, and the lexical depth uses FUSION_K. Cost stays linear in the authorized corpus.

unresolved: The grep gate's sre_parse recursion on deeply nested patterns (RecursionError vs PatternError classification) was not settled.
The superlinear cost of graph meet minimal=True pruning (prune/_articulation_points rerun per removed node) relative to the walked-set size was not measured.

candidates.title: Glob patterns compile to backtracking regex with unbounded wildcards, so one call can stall the shared event loop
candidates.description: A caller who can run glob (or grep/glean with globs) supplies a short pattern with k wildcards. Matching it against each stored name or path of length n costs O(n^k) in CPython re. The match runs synchronously on the event loop for every candidate row, before visibility filtering. A '[...]' class disables the SQL prefilter, so every row in the mount is a candidate.
candidates.root_cause: _translate emits backtracking [^/]* and (?:.+/)? for wildcards with no cap on wildcard count or pattern length. compile_glob uses Python re, not the linear-time Rust engine. The match runs inline on the loop with no deadline.
candidates.intended_behavior: Glob matching is linear in subject length, like the Rust regex engine that grep already uses, or it is bounded by a wildcard cap and a deadline, and it never blocks other callers on the shared loop.

trace.description: Accepts a caller pattern with no length or wildcard cap.
A '[' class makes _glob_like return None. The prefilter becomes an empty literal prefix plus '%', so every row is a candidate.
passes_row_filters runs the compiled regex per candidate, inline, before view.shows.
Each '*' becomes a backtracking [^/]*, compiled with Python re at line 208.

evidence.description: A '**' component becomes (?:.+/)?, which also backtracks across segments.

conditions.description: The caller can invoke glob on a mount. A fresh storage's posture lets anonymous callers do this.
The mount holds at least one row whose name or path is moderately long (tens of characters or more). Paths can be up to 1024 bytes.
The host serves several agents from one process or event loop.

execution.attacker_perspective: An agent with glob access on a shared AsyncVirtualFileSystem.
payloads: glob pattern '*?' * k + '[Q]' against a stored name 'a' * n (k=4: n=64,128; k=5: n=32,64)
instructions: In the sandbox, build an AsyncVirtualFileSystem(storage=InMemoryStorage()) and write one file whose name is n characters long.
Run a 1 ms asyncio ticker, call fs.glob(pattern), and record the glob duration and the largest gap between ticks.
execution.observed_result: k=4: 0.0071 s at n=64 and 0.0595 s at n=128. k=5: 0.0047 s at n=32 and 0.0532 s at n=64. The largest event-loop gap matched the glob time (0.056 s and 0.050 s). A direct regex check gave ratios of about 7x (k=3) and about 14x (k=4) per doubling, which fits O(n^k).

remediation.strategy: Match globs with the linear-time Rust regex engine already in vfs-core, or with a non-backtracking glob matcher. Until then, cap the wildcard count per pattern and pattern length in expand_pattern. Add a regression test that counts matcher steps or runs a fixed-size adversarial pattern under an operation-count assertion.

likelihood.reason: The input is short and every name in the mount is a target; the only requirement is glob access.

impact.reason: Each call stalls the shared event loop for every co-hosted agent. Growth is polynomial in pattern length, with no deadline.

confidence.reason: Shown end to end through the public API with bounded growth points inside the sandbox.

candidates.title: Grep context lines are duplicated per hit, so output can grow to (hit lines) × (body size)
candidates.description: In lines mode with large before_context/after_context (allowed up to 2^31-1), every hit line receives its own context span, which can be the whole body, and each span is copied into a separate PyBytes and then a str. A body where many lines match yields output quadratic in its size.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: extend_context computes one span per hit without merging overlapping contexts, python.rs copies each span, and no output-byte budget exists. CONTENT_BYTE_BUDGET bounds input batches, not output.

trace.description: Passes context sizes to verify.hit_lines with cap=max_count (None by default).
Builds a full context span per hit line.
Copies each span into a new PyBytes.

evidence.description: One span per hit; overlapping spans are not merged.

blockers: Not executed locally: the quadratic output growth has not been observed.

validation_plan.local: In the sandbox, grep a small file of L short lines that all match, with before/after context set high, at L and 2L. Sum the bytes of the returned match content and check that it grows about 4x per doubling.

hardening: Glean: limit up to 2^31-1 sets SQL LIMIT to 10×limit, so a single call can fetch every authorized chunk row; consider capping limit.
Grep: the wall-time deadline is checked only between stages or bodies, never inside one Rust match. Matching is linear-time, so this is bounded.
